title: Mock 4 · Process & Performance
blurb: Heavier on Chapters 8-10: disclosure, grievance redressal, IPS, benchmarking, TWRR and attribution, while touching every chapter.

questions.q: According to the workbook, what mainly distinguishes speculation from investment?
options: Speculation is always short term and investment always long term
Speculation pays no cognizance to the value of the asset, with profit as the sole purpose
questions.explanation: Investment involves determining value and buying assets whose intrinsic value exceeds market price; speculation pays no attention to value and focuses on profit with little regard to risk. Classifying purely by time horizon is described as not appropriate.
hints: Wrong: speculation can occur in any asset.
Wrong: the workbook says time-horizon labelling is not appropriate.
Correct: disregard for value is the key difference.
Wrong: speculation does not always lead to higher returns.

questions.q: Structured products are best described as:
options: Plain fixed deposits with a bank guarantee
Instruments combining traditional investments like bonds or equities with derivatives to create customised risk-return profiles
Government securities issued at a discount
questions.explanation: Structured products combine bonds or equities with derivatives; they are complex, may lack liquidity and carry issuer credit risk.
hints: Wrong: this describes T-bills or zero coupon G-Secs.
Wrong: index funds are passive pooled vehicles.

questions.q: The initial (upfront) margin charged by a clearing corporation is a percentage of transaction value arrived at using:
questions.explanation: Initial margin is based on the Value at Risk concept; MTM margin is the notional loss on outstanding trades.
hints: Wrong: margins are set by the clearing corporation's risk system.

questions.q: A firm has EBIT of ₹100 crore, tax rate 25%, depreciation ₹20 crore, capital expenditure ₹30 crore and increase in working capital ₹10 crore. Its FCFF is:
questions.explanation: FCFF = EBIT(1 - t) + Dep - Capex - ΔWC = 75 + 20 - 30 - 10 = ₹55 crore.
hints: Wrong: ignores tax and the WC change.
Wrong: this is only EBIT after tax.

questions.q: Which valuation multiple is best suited to capital-intensive industries and to comparing firms with different debt structures?
questions.explanation: EV/EBITDA suits capital-intensive industries and companies with different debt structures since EBITDA is unaffected by capital structure.
hints: Wrong: P/B suits banks and financials.
Wrong: not discussed as a multiple for this purpose.
Wrong: P/S suits loss-makers and low-margin businesses.

questions.q: Why may an analyst prefer the Price to Sales ratio for a young company?
options: Because the company is not yet earning profits and sales are less prone to manipulation
Because book value is always zero for young companies
questions.explanation: P/S is used as sales are less prone to manipulation and is useful for companies not yet earning profits or in high-volume low-margin businesses.
hints: Wrong: P/S uses market capitalisation in the numerator.

questions.q: Callable bonds expose the investor to a higher level of:
questions.explanation: Issuers call bonds when rates fall, forcing investors to reinvest at lower rates: reinvestment risk.
hints: Wrong: callability does not change default probability.

questions.q: In a fixed-for-floating interest rate swap, what is exchanged on each settlement date?
options: Only the interest amounts computed on the notional principal
questions.explanation: The principal (notional amount) is never exchanged; only the interest on it is exchanged on each settlement date.
hints: Wrong: swaps exchange cash flows, not shares.

questions.q: Factor (smart beta) funds are described in the workbook as falling:
questions.explanation: Factor funds use rules (passive-like) but select stocks systematically and frequently (active-like), so they fall between active and passive funds.
hints: Wrong: they are mutual fund categories.
Wrong: they are not purely passive.

questions.q: Within how many days must a portfolio manager take adequate steps for redressal of investor grievances, as stated in the workbook?
questions.explanation: The PM shall take adequate steps for redressal of grievances within 21 calendar days of receipt of the complaint and keep SEBI informed.
hints: Wrong: 7 working days is for STRs to FIU.
Wrong: 30 days is for quarterly tax reports.

questions.q: The compliance officer of a portfolio manager, on observing a non-compliance, shall:
options: Inform only the Board of the PM
Immediately and independently report it to SEBI
questions.explanation: The compliance officer shall immediately and independently report to SEBI any non-compliance observed.
hints: Correct: immediate and independent reporting to SEBI.

questions.q: Off-market transfers in a client's account by a PM are permitted in all of the following cases EXCEPT:
options: Settlement of the client's own trades
Providing margin for the client's own positions
With specific client consent for each transaction
Transferring securities to the PM's own account for safekeeping
questions.explanation: Permitted: client's own trade settlement, margin/collateral for client positions, unlisted securities dealings, specific consent per transaction, reasons specified by SEBI. A PM must never hold client securities in its own name.
hints: Correct: not permitted; PM cannot hold client securities in its own name.

questions.q: In the Disclosure Document, the performance of the portfolio manager for the last three years (for discretionary PMs) must be computed using:
questions.explanation: Part II (dynamic section) requires PM performance for the last three years, with discretionary PM performance indicators calculated using TWRR.
hints: Wrong: not a performance measure for this purpose.

questions.q: When reporting performance to an individual investor, the portfolio manager must present for each investment approach:
options: Only the TWRR of the investment approach
The investor's XIRR along with the minimum, maximum and median XIRR across all investors in that approach
questions.explanation: PMs present XIRR for each IA the investor invests in, with min, max and median XIRR across all investors, plus TWRR and benchmark trailing return separately.
hints: Wrong: TWRR alone is for advertising/IA performance.
Correct: XIRR with min, max and median.

questions.q: Under the Online Dispute Resolution mechanism, which stages are free of cost for investors?
questions.explanation: The first two stages, pre-conciliation and conciliation, are free of cost for investors; arbitration produces a binding award.
hints: Wrong: arbitration is not stated to be free.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of the Investment Policy Statement listed in the workbook?
options: Guaranteeing a minimum return to the investor
Protecting investors from inappropriate or unethical decisions
questions.explanation: The IPS sets expectations, provides an evaluation framework and protects investors, but it never guarantees returns.
hints: Wrong: this is a listed purpose.
Wrong: this is a listed purpose.
Correct: IPS does not guarantee returns.
Wrong: this is a listed purpose.

questions.q: If a portfolio manager changes the strategy or benchmark tagged to an investment approach, it must:
options: Charge an exit load to departing investors
Seek approval from each investor's bank
Offer existing investors an option to exit without exit load
questions.explanation: Tagging can be changed only after offering subscribers of the IA an option to exit without any exit load; the old track record cannot be used for performance reporting.
hints: Wrong: investors must be offered an exit.
Wrong: the exit must be load-free.

questions.q: For near-term, high-priority goals, the workbook suggests investing in:
options: Cash equivalents or fixed income maturing to match the goal date
questions.explanation: Near-term high-priority goals use cash equivalents or fixed-income instruments with maturity dates matching the goal date.
hints: Wrong: too volatile for a near-term must-have goal.

questions.q: Which of the following is a challenge of portfolio rebalancing?
options: It may trigger capital gains taxes and transaction costs
It enforces buy low, sell high
It keeps the portfolio aligned with risk tolerance
questions.explanation: Challenges include tax implications, transaction costs, market timing difficulty and emotional bias; the other options are benefits.

questions.q: A portfolio's sub-period returns between client cash flows are 10%, -5% and 8%. The TWRR for the whole period is approximately:
In performance attribution, the formula Σ (Wp - Wb) x Rb measures the:
questions.explanation: Allocation effect = Σ(Wp - Wb) x Rb: the impact of over/under-weighting relative to the benchmark.
hints: Wrong: total is the sum of all three.

questions.q: Mr. A stayed in India for 75 days in the current financial year and for 400 days in total during the preceding four financial years. As per the workbook's test, he is:
questions.explanation: An individual is resident if in India for 182 days or more, OR at least 60 days in the year and 365 days or more in the preceding four years. 75 and 400 satisfy the second test.
hints: Wrong: the basic test only decides residency; RNOR needs further conditions.

questions.q: Losses from derivatives trading through a PMS can be set off against:
options: Other business or non-salaried income in the same year
questions.explanation: Derivative business losses can be set off against other business or non-salaried income in the same year, but not against salary.
hints: Wrong: too restrictive and not stated.

questions.q: A designated person who is a connected person of a listed company and is permitted to trade in its securities shall not execute a contra trade for a period of at least:
questions.explanation: The code of conduct shall specify a period not less than six months for contra trades (not less than two months for mutual fund units).
hints: Wrong: this is the pre-clearance execution window.
Wrong: this applies to mutual fund units.

questions.q: Under the PFUTP Regulations, which of the following is deemed a manipulative or unfair trade practice?
options: Buying shares after reading the published annual report
Hedging a portfolio with index futures
Knowingly creating a false or misleading appearance of trading in a security
Selling shares to rebalance a portfolio
questions.explanation: Knowingly indulging in an act which creates a false or misleading appearance of trading is deemed manipulative, fraudulent or unfair.
hints: Wrong: legitimate use of public information.
